rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '2' to '1' ONLY in the comment text '// Ensure block size is power of 2 for reduction'. Comments are stripped during CUDA compilation and have zero effect on executable code. The actual BLOCK_SIZE computation '1 << (int)log2f(BLOCK_SIZE)' is identical in both versions.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation only affects a comment string, changing 'power of 2' to 'power of 1' in line 119. Comments in C++/CUDA are completely ignored by the compiler and have no effect on the generated machine code. The actual computational logic—including the BLOCK_SIZE calculation, kernel launch parameters, and all arithmetic operations—remains byte-for-byte identical. Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise identical outputs across 112 rounds because the compiled CUDA kernels are functionally equivalent. No input value can distinguish between two programs with identical compiled code.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable: The mutation is in a comment, which has no effect on program execution. The compiled CUDA code is identical between original and mutant. No test input can distinguish between programs with identical compiled binaries.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should filter out comment-only mutations from the candidate pool, as they are always semantically equivalent and waste testing resources. Consider implementing a pre-filter that detects mutations to comment tokens or string literals within comment blocks.
